video_title: Mike D’Antoni Tells the Real Story Behind Linsanity & Coaching Harden

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeremy Lin's 10-day contract and the decision to play him
quotes.excerpt: He's on a 10-day contract. He's ready to get released. Maybe we should give him a chance.
quotes.quote: He's on a 10-day contract. He's ready to get released. This was on a Friday or Thursday before Friday's game. They go, Jeremy's got something, he works out really well. Maybe we should give him a chance. I go, we're going to release him on Tuesday. So if we're going to give him a chance, we better give him a chance.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on his upbringing in West Virginia
quotes.excerpt: I grew up in a little coal mining town. We just played basketball, played sports.
quotes.quote: I grew up in a little coal mining town. We just played basketball, played sports. It used to call us the 10-2 boys because the sun got up at 10 and we set at 2. So that was, we just played sports and basketball was always the main sport. So I just got lucky.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Amar'e Stoudemire's mindset and work ethic
quotes.excerpt: Once you put your mind to something, man, it's good. You've overcome a lot of injuries.
quotes.quote: The thing about you, which impressed me, is your mindset. Once you put your mind to something, man, it's good. And that's why a lot of us coaches, the Phoenix Suns, then New York Knicks, appreciate you, because you've overcome a lot of injuries that you had to focus on your craft. I need a jump shot, then you work all summer, you get a jump shot. I need to get my handle stronger, you work all summer, you get a handle stronger. So, that's impressive what you did.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on his talented team in Italy
quotes.excerpt: We had Moses Malone, Marvin Barnes, Lionel Hollins, Caldwell Jones, Ron Boone, Freddy Lewis.
quotes.quote: We had Moses Malone, Marvin Barnes, Lionel Hollins, Caldwell Jones, Ron Boone, Freddy Lewis. We had some studs on that team. And there was only six teams. So we'd play maybe Dr. J was playing on one, Dan Issel and Louie Dampier at Kentucky. Nate Archibald, I got to see in his prime right when he started. Nate Archibald was unbelievable. I'd be on the bench sometimes and he would do one of his classy, which everybody sees now and they think, oh, that's nothing. That was the first time anybody's ever seen that and the whole bench would erupt.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Marvin Barnes' talent and off-court troubles
quotes.excerpt: Marvin Barnes was the prototype for the stretch four now. Marvin would go, he'd get 40 a night.
quotes.quote: One of the under-appreciated guys is Marvin Barnes, because he got in a little trouble in college where he took a tire and somebody, you know, wasn't good. But funny, and man, he was the prototype for the stretch four now. Marvin would go, he'd get 40 a night. This guy could play. If he didn't let his troubles off the court get to him, and it was, you know, back in the 70s, the NBA and the ABA, it was kind of tough on and off the court, but he was a talent.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni's transition to head coaching in Italy
quotes.excerpt: I'm 40 years old. And you don't make a lot of money in Europe. You make good money.
quotes.quote: I'm 40 years old. And you don't make a lot of money in Europe. You make good money, but you know, 40 years old, now what am I going to do? Do I go back to school? Do I become a coach? You know, I have no idea. So I'm lying around in Myrtle Beach thinking, I got to do something. And the phone rings and my team I just left called me up and goes, Mike, you want to be the head coach? I go, well, yeah.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni's tactical shift with the Phoenix Suns
quotes.excerpt: My leading scorer of the team, who's a post backup four, he goes to the bench.
quotes.quote: I went to the coaches meeting, I said, here's what we're doing. My leading scorer of the team, who's a post backup four, he goes to the bench. And they're like looking at me like I'm crazy because he's the leading scorer. So I said, no, he goes to the bench, I move the three to the four, the five is good because he's a runner and pick and roll guy, great point guard, and I'm putting three shooters around him and here we go.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the '7 Seconds or Less' moniker
quotes.excerpt: I asked Jack McCallum who wrote the book 7 Seconds or Less, where'd you get the title?
quotes.quote: I asked Jack McCallum who wrote the book 7 Seconds or Less, where'd you get the title? Because I don't remember me saying to you guys, hey, 7 seconds or less. I was good with 10 seconds or less. I didn't care, just as long as we scored. He said, I don't really know. I think some of your assistant coaches were saying it because you'd be watching film and it'd be up on the shot clock and yeah, that was less than 7 seconds.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Amar'e Stoudemire's dunking ability
quotes.excerpt: How many times did you would dunk over somebody like Yao Ming or Hakeem Olajuwon?
quotes.quote: You know how many times like when you would dunk the ball, that was ridiculous. I mean, how many times did you would dunk over somebody like Yao Ming or Hakeem Olajuwon or just go on and on and on. And the rim would be just going crazy. It'd be shaking.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Joe Johnson's efficiency and shooting
quotes.excerpt: You realize Joe Johnson shot 47% from threes that year? I knew he was good.
quotes.quote: You realize Joe Johnson shot 47% from threes that year? I knew he was good, but 47% is ridiculous.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the misconception of NBA players
quotes.excerpt: 99% of the players are overachievers, good guys, and work and put on a nice product.
quotes.quote: I think that's one thing that the people have misconstrued about the NBA, because you hear about the bad, bad stuff. And that's like nothing. I mean, 99% of the players are overachievers, good guys, and work and put on a nice product every night. So people would only concentrate a little bit on the 5%, but we had some great players.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the Linsanity phenomenon
quotes.excerpt: Can you believe how much energy was in that building for Linsanity?
quotes.quote: Can you believe how much energy was in that building for Linsanity? I can only imagine what the playoffs were this year, you know, what they did. But the Linsanity was crazy.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on leaving the Phoenix Suns
quotes.excerpt: I got really frustrated we couldn't get over the hump and we were right there.
quotes.quote: I got really frustrated we couldn't get over the hump and we were right there. And it was San Antonio who only had three Hall of Fame players. They were good. And Pop does a great job obviously. So it just the frustration built and that year we didn't resign Shawn and it just felt like, you know, I've had my run here. And to be honest with you, and looking back, sometimes you make decisions you don't know why, you know. It's like, my son was entering the eighth grade and I was talking with my wife, I go, look, he's in the eighth grade. If I'm going to make a move, I'm going to do it before he gets to high school because once he gets in high school, I'm not making a move.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the importance of family in coaching
quotes.excerpt: You always put them first, no matter what. And I think as an organization, we tried to.
quotes.quote: You always put them first, no matter what. And I think as an organization, we tried to. And we always made sure the wives were involved, whether it's in the community or whatever. So that helps them. If they're engaged with the team, it helps the player to go home to a happy house.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the difficulty of coaching
quotes.excerpt: One of my favorite guys is probably Joey Crawford, who's coming into the Hall with us.
quotes.quote: One of my favorite guys is probably Joey Crawford, who's coming into the Hall with us. He was great. I mean, and that's what I like, you know, it's referees with personalities that can take crap from me but also give me crap. I'm fine with. But the ones that don't take anything and are too stuck up, they're the ones that get under my skin.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the challenges of coaching
quotes.excerpt: I remember he was reading a book about Tim Donaghy who later admitted that he was cheating.
quotes.quote: I remember he was reading a book about Tim Donaghy who later admitted that he was cheating and fixing games. And then it says that he was involved in our games against the Spurs in the playoffs. I don't know, it's crazy. That's messed up.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the impact of injuries on his teams
quotes.excerpt: It just it just, you know, it wore Steve out as we went on with the playoffs.
quotes.quote: It just it just, you know, it wore Steve out as we went on with the playoffs. And losing Joe was really hurt us. And Jimmy Jackson did a good job. He came in and played well. But it just it just, you know, it wore Steve out as we went on with the playoffs. And losing Joe was really hurt us.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on the evolution of NBA analytics
quotes.excerpt: We were doing it with just stats. You know, just, you know, how many you made, whatever.
quotes.quote: We were doing it with just stats. You know, just, you know, how many you made, whatever. They're doing it now with analytics. And analytics is telling them that's the way to go. And we kind of knew it just by seat of our pants, but, you know, when we shoot, I don't remember our team would shoot 33 threes and I'm going home at night thinking, is that too many? You know, right. I know. Right. Should we did should we post up more? Right. And if I had analytics back then, we'd have been shooting about 45.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on Kobe Bryant's work ethic
quotes.excerpt: He has a mindset like yours, that gets something done, he's getting it done.
quotes.quote: He has a mindset like yours, that gets something done, he's getting it done. And he would play through injuries and he would, to be honest with you, his last year when he tore his Achilles, I couldn't get him out of the game. He wouldn't come out. He's like looking at me like I'm crazy. He's not coming out because he's going to show everybody what it takes to get to the playoffs and he individually willed us to it.

quotes.speaker: Mike D'Antoni
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike D'Antoni on James Harden's playmaking ability
quotes.excerpt: James needs to be the point guard, because he had, I was watching tape and he you.
quotes.quote: James needs to be the point guard, because he had, I was watching tape and he you, I knew that he he kind of can set the table. And man, he was a lot better than I ever thought he could be. He was he was incredible.
